questions.question: In SQL, the WHERE clause is used to filter groups after aggregation.
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before aggregation; HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY.

questions.question: A pandas DataFrame's `describe()` method includes the median by default.
questions.explanation: `describe()` shows the 50% percentile which is the median.

questions.question: The `groupby().filter()` method in pandas can remove entire groups based on a condition.
questions.explanation: `filter()` returns a subset of groups that satisfy a function, effectively dropping groups.

questions.question: In SQL, `SELECT DISTINCT` can be used with multiple columns to return unique combinations.
questions.explanation: `DISTINCT` applies to all selected columns, returning unique rows.

questions.question: `df.dropna()` drops only rows where all values are NaN.
questions.explanation: By default, `dropna()` drops any row that has at least one NaN. Use `how='all'` to drop only if all values are NaN.

questions.question: In pandas, you can pass a dictionary to `rename(columns={...})` to rename specific columns.
questions.explanation: The `columns` parameter accepts a dict mapping old names to new names.

questions.question: The SQL query `SELECT * FROM orders WHERE amount > (SELECT AVG(amount) FROM orders);` is valid.
questions.explanation: Subqueries are allowed in the WHERE clause.
